title: One Simulated Machine Step During a Sweep
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $y,x$ be Boolean words, let $bits$ be a selector-bit assignment for $M$, let $P$ be a valid input-head position for $y$, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, and let $\tau_C,\tau_O:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{none},\mathrm{some} (\mathrm{false}),\mathrm{some} (\mathrm{true})\}$ with head positions $z_C,z_O\in\mathbb{Z}$. If $c$ is in state $q$, the Boolean tag $b$ correctly marks the input-head boundary of $c$, and the $C$ buffer contains true at position $z_C$, then there is a tag $b'$ correctly marking the input-head boundary after one step of $M$ such that one step of the simulator, started in its decode state with the output register obtained from $c$'s output, produces the lcfg configuration for that successor machine configuration. In that resulting configuration, the $C$ buffer is updated at $z_C$ to false and its head moves to $z_C-1$; the $O$ buffer and its head position are retained.
caveat: The conclusion relies on the simulator's defined configuration constructors and transition states, whose full meanings are not supplied as informal definitions.
